get_absence_period.name: get_absence_period

parameters.name: id

data.description: A period of time with an associated absence type.

id.description: A unique identifier for an Absence Type.

approval.description: Information related to the approval status of a period.

status.description:
The approval status of this period.
* PENDING: This period is awaiting approval.
* APPROVED: This period has been approved.
* DELETION_PENDING: The creator of this period has deleted it. The deletion has not yet been approved.
* SUBSTITUTE_REQUESTED: The creator of this period specified a substitute employee to cover for them. The
  substitute has not yet accepted this request.

comment.description: A comment attached to this period.

created_at.description:
The time at which this period was created. This is a UTC timestamp and is unrelated to the `timezone_id`
field.

ends_at.description:
This object represents the end of the absence period. It may be null for periods which are
ongoing and do not have a defined end. For example, `ends_at` will generally be unknown for long term sick
leave.

date_time.description: An RFC3339 date and timestamp without a timezone offset.

type.description:
Determines whether this period ends after the first half or second half of the day. See the
description of the `starts_from` field for a detailed explanation.

id.description: A unique identifier for this period.
A unique identifier for a Person.

starts_from.description:
This object represents the beginning of the absence period.

The `starts_from` and `ends_at` fields specify the *calendar duration* of the absence period, without any
consideration of a person's working schedule or public holidays. There are 3 different ways that this time
range is handled:
  - For periods with a DAILY `AbsenceType`: the start and end must be at midnight in the provided timezone. The
    `type` field may specify that the period starts or ends half way through the day. This information is used
    when computing the absence balance. It cannot accurately determine the exact time that a person will stop
    or start working because the midpoint of a day depends on a person's working schedule.
  - For periods with an HOURLY `AbsenceType` with duration < 24 hours: the start and end time have minute
  granularity and specify the exact period of the absence. The `type` field is not meaningful in this case.
  - For periods with an HOURLY `AbsenceType` with duration > 24 hours: the start and end time fields and the
  `type` fields behave the same as with DAILY `AbsenceType`s.

**Timezones**

All dates are provided as local times in the locale specified by the `timezone_id` field. The timestamps have
no offset.

In all cases there is validation of these constraints on the server side.

date_time.description: An RFC3339 date and timestamp without a timezone offset.

type.description:

of the `starts_from` field for a detailed explanation.

timezone_id.description:
A timezone ID string, as defined in https://www.iana.org/time-zones. The start and end dates of the period
are specified in this timezone.

updated_at.description:
The time at which this period was last updated. This is a UTC timestamp and is unrelated to the `timezone_id`
field.

data.description:
A daily breakdown of an absence period indicating how much absence balance is consumed for each day of
the absence period.

There will be one entry for each day in the absence period, ordered chronologically. If an absence
period is ongoing (it has `ends_at = null`), breakdowns will exist for every completed day up to the
current day.

items.description: Details about how a single day within an absence period affects absence balance accounting.

date.description: The day which this breakdown describes, in the timezone referenced by the periods `timezone_id` field.

effective_duration.description:
The amount of time that is subtracted from the employee's absence balance as a result of this day in the
absence period.

This number takes into account the working days, hours and public holidays of the employee. For example
it will be 0 on Saturdays and Sundays if the employee does not work at weekends.

unit.description:
The units used in the `value` field.
* DAY: `value` represents the effective duration as a fractional number of days such as 1.0 or 0.5.
* MINUTE: `value` represents the effective duration as a number of minutes, such as 60 or 480

value.description: The effective duration of the period, in the units specified by `unit`.

list_people_ending_probation.description: Find everyone whose probation period ends soon, with their manager. Returns each active person whose probation ends today or within the number of days you choose (14 unless you say otherwise), with their name, email, job title, department, start date, the day probation ends, how many days are left, and their manager's name and email. The same people come grouped by manager, each group with the manager's email and a ready-made text list and HTML table of their people, so emailing each manager their own list is this step, a loop over 'by_manager' and a send: no filtering, grouping or lookup steps. People with no manager, or whose manager has no email in Personio, are listed separately in 'without_manager_email'. The step reads every page itself. Personio only gives probation dates one person at a time, so it reads each active person's employment record, which can take a minute or more on an account with many hundreds of people. 'Today' is the date in UTC. The connection needs Read access to Employees in Personio, with the probation end date, supervisor and position shared.

description: Manage people and projects, and read employments, absences, attendance and reports in Personio.

personio_new_absence_period_trigger.description: Runs for each new absence (time off such as vacation or sick leave) booked in Personio, with the person's name, the kind of time off and its first and last day ready to use. Set Approval to approved to run only once an absence is approved, the right choice for a team calendar or an announcement: a request made first and approved later starts the workflow when it is approved. Absences already there (or already approved) when the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.absence_type_category: Beta. Personio's own category for that kind of time off, in capitals: SICK_LEAVE for sick leave and PAID_VACATION for paid vacation; other kinds of time off have categories of their own. It stays the same whatever your company calls the absence type, so compare this (is it SICK_LEAVE?) rather than the name. Blank if Personio gives none.
output.absence_type_name: Beta. The kind of time off, as your company named it in Personio, such as Paid vacation or Sick leave.
output.all_day: Beta. true when the absence is booked in whole or half days, false when it is booked in hours within a day.
output.approval_status: Beta. Where the absence stands: approved; pending (waiting for approval); substitute requested (waiting for a colleague to agree to cover); or deletion pending (the person asked to cancel it and that is waiting for approval).
output.comment: Beta. The note written on the absence, if any.
output.dates_display: Beta. The whole absence in one phrase for a message: Mar 3, 2025 to Mar 5, 2025, or just Mar 3, 2025 for a single day.
output.end_date: Beta. The last day away as a plain date, such as 2025-03-05. The person is still away on this day. Blank when the absence has no end yet, as with long sick leave.
output.end_date_exclusive: Beta. The day after the last day away, such as 2025-03-06: the end date an all-day event in Google Calendar or Outlook wants, since they end an all-day event on the day after. Blank when the absence has no end yet.
output.end_display: Beta. The last day written the same way, such as Mar 5, 2025, with (morning only) added when the absence ends at midday. Blank when the absence has no end yet.
output.half_day_end: Beta. true when the absence ends at midday, so the person is away only for the morning of the last day. Otherwise false.
output.half_day_start: Beta. true when the absence starts at midday, so the person is away only for the afternoon of the first day. Otherwise false.
